title: Processing model of track element handles parent media element in confusing way
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

This might be us having trouble to reading the spec, but in both ways we can read the specification, we are unsure whether the behavior is desirable.

In http://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/#start-the-track-processing-model at step 5 it calls https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/#await-a-stable-state where the synchronous steps 6 to 8 are executed. The order of execution was not clear to me at first, as I thought it was the following:

1. Synchronous section
2. Await a stable state
3. Parallel part

But rereading the spec again, I think the intended order is:

1. Await a stable state
2. Synchronous section
3. Parallel part

In the first case, step 8 does not make sense, since step 3 already checks if the parent is a media element. Hence we think that the second case is correct. That would make more sense, since after awaiting a stable state, it could be that the track element no longer has a parent media element.

However, why does the algorithm proceed in this case? If the track element has no media element, the request that consequently would get fetched in step 10.4 wouldn't affect a media element and thus all of that logic would be redundant.

Therefore, if our reading is correct and it is the second case, shouldn't we instead abort the algorithm if the parent is no longer a media element in step 8?
